advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm StorePaths.git_dir using self.canonical (vs raw str(tracker)) preserves push_state marker behavior for symlinked worktree views, and add a symlinked-view test for push_state._marker_path.
evidence: old push_state._git_dir: `dot_git = os.path.join(str(tracker), ".git")` and `target = os.path.join(str(tracker), target)` (removed diff hunk)
ABSENCE: tests/unit/store/test_store_paths.py git_dir tests all build the tracker via os.path.realpath(tmp_path) with no symlink, so the canonical-vs-raw distinction for push_state is untested
advisory.finding: StorePaths.git_dir resolves its base through self.canonical (os.path.realpath) whereas the collapsed push_state._git_dir used the raw str(tracker); this is a behavior change on the git-dir derivation, contradicting the commit's 'No behaviour changes' claim. For a relative gitdir: pointer the resolution base differs (canonical vs raw tracker), and no test exercises push_state._marker_path under a symlinked worktree view.
scenarios: push_state marker path derived from a worktree-view tracker whose .git is a gitfile with a relative gitdir: pointer

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either wire a real caller to StorePaths.git_common_dir or drop it until a consumer exists.
evidence: search for `git_common_dir` returns only src/rebar/_store/paths.py:136 and the two test references; no production consumer
commit message: 'Two further git-dir parsers (gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir, lock._gitdir) ... are deliberately left untouched'
advisory.finding: StorePaths.git_common_dir is a net-new public derivation with no production caller — the commit explicitly leaves the two existing git-dir parsers (gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir, lock._gitdir) untouched, so git_common_dir collapses nothing and is only exercised by the new test.
scenarios: future maintainer unsure whether git_common_dir has a caller or is dead API

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Harden the tracker-sibling guard to also catch multi-line dirname(...)+'.rebar' derivations (e.g. scan a normalized/joined window rather than a single physical line).
evidence: `for lineno, line in enumerate(... splitlines())` then `if '".rebar"' not in line ...: continue` and `if not any(atom in line for atom in _PARENT_ATOMS): continue` (tests/unit/store/test_store_paths.py:204-208)
the guard's verdict (empty offenders == pass) is produced identically whether no offending line exists or an offender was split across lines and thus never matched
advisory.finding: The construct-uniqueness guard _tracker_sibling_offenders matches only when '.rebar' and a parent-step (os.path.dirname( / .parent) appear on the SAME source line; a copy-pasted derivation split across two lines (e.g. dirname assigned on one line, joined with '.rebar' on the next) escapes the scan, so the guard can report 'clean' when the class has in fact re-entered.
scenarios: a sixth copy re-derives .rebar over two lines; guard stays green

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test for StorePaths.git_common_dir covering the commondir pointer, the no-commondir (git_dir IS common dir) case, and the empty/unreadable fallback.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/paths.py:136: `def git_common_dir(self) -> str:` reads a `commondir` file and has three outcomes (resolved pointer, empty→git_dir, OSError→git_dir)
tests/unit/store/test_store_paths.py:98: `sp.git_common_dir,` is only inside the isinstance(str) loop of test_store_paths_exposes_the_documented_derivations
search: `git_common_dir` appears only at paths.py:136 and the two type-check lines in the test — no behavioral assertion and no production caller
advisory.finding: The newly introduced StorePaths.git_common_dir property has no behavioral test: its commondir-pointer resolution, empty-target fallback, and OSError fallback branches are only exercised by an isinstance(str) type check, so a regression in any branch would pass silently.
scenarios: A linked worktree whose git dir holds a commondir file pointing at the main checkout
A commondir file containing a relative path resolved against git_dir

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a git_dir test using a relative `gitdir:` pointer to cover the relative branch of _resolve_pointer.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/paths.py:76: `_resolve_pointer(target, base)` joins non-absolute targets against base then normpaths
search for `gitdir: ..` (a relative pointer) in tests: (no matches)
advisory.finding: The relative-pointer branch of _resolve_pointer (`if not os.path.isabs(target): target = os.path.join(base, target)` then normpath) is never exercised — every gitdir/commondir test uses an absolute target — even though relative `gitdir:` pointers are the common real-world shape for linked worktrees and submodules.
scenarios: A linked worktree whose .git file contains a relative `gitdir: ../.git/worktrees/foo` pointer
